options: A separate report that opens when a user selects a link in another paginated report
A section of the same report that expands in place when toggled
A report embedded permanently inside another report's layout
A cached copy of a report stored for offline viewing
questions.explain: A drillthrough report is genuinely separate from the main report — clicking a link (on a text box, image, or chart point) opens it, rather than expanding anything in place.

questions.q: When is a drillthrough report's data actually retrieved?
options: Only when the user clicks the link that opens it
At the exact same time the main report runs, regardless of clicks
The moment the report is published to the Report Server
Every time the main report's parameters change, even without a click
questions.explain: Drillthrough data is lazy — it isn't queried until the user clicks the link. That's what makes drillthrough reports typically cheaper to run than subreports.

questions.q: On the Action tab of an item's Properties dialog, which option turns it into a drillthrough link?
options: Go to report
Go to bookmark
Go to URL
Go to parameter
questions.explain: Go to report is the Action-tab option for drillthrough links; Go to bookmark and Go to URL serve the other two link types covered in Lesson 29.

questions.q: What is the single most common reason a drillthrough action fails when a user clicks it?
options: A parameter name in the parameter grid doesn't match the target report's parameter exactly, including case
The main report and drillthrough report use different color themes
The drillthrough report has more than one dataset
The main report was published before the drillthrough report
questions.explain: Parameter names must match the target report's expected parameters exactly, case included. A mismatch or a missing expected parameter causes the drillthrough to fail at run time.

questions.q: What's required for a drillthrough set up as a "report action" (rather than a URL action)?
options: The drillthrough report must be published to the same report server as the main report, though it can be in a different folder
The drillthrough report must be in the exact same folder as the main report
The drillthrough report must have zero parameters
The drillthrough report must be embedded in the main report's RDL file
questions.explain: A report action requires both reports live on the same report server — different folders are fine. A URL action, by contrast, can target a fully qualified URL anywhere.
